track: B (our data: data/train_ours.parquet / test_ours.parquet; run-(a) ToU clusters relabelled to the authors' 0-3; ERA5 temperatures; Tariffs.xlsx 'loc' tariffs)

matched_to_authors_cluster_3.relabel_rule: Hungarian on raw cluster-mean correlations (agrees with deviation and contingency matching)

selection.selection_metric: test_mse_post = authors' compute_mse on the 92 test days (posterior z, one draw per day, fixed RNG seed 0, common to all restarts); lowest wins

pca.claim: Sec. V-B-2: a PCA on the consumption data: 4 components explain more than 80% of the variance
pca.data: power_consump_ours.parquet: 365 daily 48-half-hour profiles per cluster (cluster-mean kWh, our run-(a) clusters relabelled to the authors' 0-3)
pca.method: PCA = SVD of the column-centred matrix (sklearn PCA cross-check on raw data); 'uncentred' = share of the total sum of squares (no centring)

extra_temperature_pca_48temps_plus_smoot.note: context only (ERA5 temperatures); the temperature PCA claim is checked by the conditions task

effects.definition: diff = mean over the 200 samples of (scenario - Normal), per test day and slot, kWh per household per half-hour (same z draws in both scenarios); region stats average the slots of the region; 'pct' is relative to the Normal mean over the same slots and days

effects_all_restarts.definition: per restart: same scenario construction and z draws as cvae_scenario_effects.json; region means in % of the Normal scenario over the same slots; claimed signs from Sec. VII-C

mirror_check.purpose: run-time evidence that Track B uses exactly Track A's settings and code paths

gam_code_reproduces_trackA_cluster3.note: this refit ran with OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1 vs 4 in 11_trackA_gam.py, so rounding-level differences would be acceptable; anything above 1e-8 kWh would not

verify_retrain.definition: retrain from scratch with lib.cvae_torch.run_restart_job (same job keys as the train stage), compare with the stored restart

deviations_from_upstream: PyTorch float64 instead of TF2/Keras float64 (same layers, loss, initialiser family, Keras-Adam update rule).
Each restart uses its own seed (seeds 0..49) for the Glorot init and the reparameterisation noise; upstream reuses one glorot_uniform(seed=0) object and unseeded tf.random.normal.
Fresh Adam per restart; upstream shares ONE Adam instance across all restarts and clusters.
Selection metric evaluated with a fixed RNG (seed 0, common to all restarts); upstream draws are unseeded.
Generation: z drawn with numpy (default_rng([20200801, cluster])), same z for real-condition samples and the three tariff scenarios (common random numbers).
trackB_data_differences_vs_trackA: households: our 1,032 ToU households (the authors' 1,007 + 25), clustered by our run-(a) pipeline; ARI 0.58 with the authors' partition; sizes 285/299/299/149 vs 325/295/229/158
temperatures: ERA5 (central London, bilinear) instead of NOAA; derived conditions r >= 0.915 with the authors'
tariffs: Tariffs.xlsx in the physically right alignment ('loc'); differs from the authors' schedule on 17 days
same 273/92 train/test dates as the authors'
run_notes: The 200 restarts were trained in two invocations of the train stage: 143 (seeds 0-35 of clusters 0-2, 0-34 of cluster 3) by a first process that stopped before finishing, then the remaining 57 by a second one (finished restarts are skipped; unfinished ones leave no record and are trained afresh). Three restarts of the first invocation were in progress while the machine was suspended and record ~4,640 s of wall time as runtime_train_s; use the per-cluster runtime_train_s_median. The verify stage retrains the four selected restarts and those three from scratch and finds them bitwise identical (cvae_verify_retrain.json).
